batches.family: Authority review intake route and store (0C.1 REV)

items.explanation: requireAdverseMembers checks every named adverse party is an active member of the organization (one generic refusal, no per-identity oracle) before anything is written. Real-SQL pglite test.

Per-member intake is serialised with an advisory lock; a repeat of an identical open review returns that review (200, alreadyOpen) instead of another append-only row; a daily cap of 10 raises REVIEW_INTAKE_LIMIT answered 429 with Retry-After. pglite and route tests.
readBoundedBody enforces a 2 KiB cap by declared length and by streamed length, cancelling the stream, before JSON parsing; 413 otherwise.
Both handlers call withRLSContext({ organizationId }) with the organization the route resolved, so the database context cannot be a second resolution.
reviewErrorResponse maps ApiError to 401/403 and logs any other failure with logger.error, answering a structured INTERNAL_ERROR 500 that does not echo the cause.
An oversight read persists review.oversight.read with the disclosed review ids and the privileged count through persistAtomicAudit in the same transaction; an own-only list records nothing.

batches.family: Mobile inbox, devices, push, negotiations and meeting rooms (0B.9 MOB), with shared CRUD-factory mechanisms (writableFields, omitFromResponse, ownerMayDelete)

items.explanation: The swallowing try/catch is removed from the list and count reads, so a failed read is a failure; page and limit are parsed strictly (400).

Strict schema bounds title, message, type, label, link (same-site path only) and data size and requires a future expiry; the author is stored in data.origin (client origin overwritten); 100 per hour per steward; the audit carries a content digest.
Only a real boolean is accepted; readAt is set when read and cleared when unread; the audit stores a boolean.
The route states it tests the inbox only, reports each channel's real state, reuses a recent unread test row, and expires new rows after an hour.
Registration is at the member floor with an allow-list of fields, a platform check and a token check, so unknown platforms no longer reach the database enum as a 500.
items.remaining: A user with no profiles row still fails the foreign key as a 500.

items.explanation: Both device tables now have an owner removal route (PATCH preferences and DELETE for push devices, DELETE for mobile devices), audited.
items.remaining: The two tables are not consolidated, and no sender reads either table (services/fcm-service.ts and lib/mobile/mobile-engine.ts remain unimported by any route or worker).

items.explanation: omitFromResponse removes the push token from every push-device response; the sync route projects an explicit safe column list that excludes the token, the jailbreak flag and the compliance columns.

The route accepts the body its only caller sends (a browser needs no token), says in every response that no synchronization was performed, and the Sync now button shows success only when the response says it synced.
items.remaining: No synchronization is implemented: mobile_sync_queue is still never read or written.

items.explanation: Re-registration updates organizationId, a token held by another device is a 409, and every field is length-validated against its column before any write.

Web push subscription has no store and no sender, so both routes answer 501 and read or write nothing, instead of CRUD over the campaign table that failed and left the client believing it had subscribed.
The only paths that served push_notifications to a member are removed; the table is no longer classified for generic CRUD, so it is DENIED by default.
No route can create a push_notifications row any more, so a row cannot be written as sent with delivery counters.

The mobile path runs the same handlers as /api/notifications (shared in lib/notifications/inbox-handlers.ts, each path behind its own visible guard), so it serves the in-app inbox (own rows) instead of the scheduled queue table.
Create now goes through the inbox POST, which checks the recipient is a member of the organization, validates input and cannot set a sent state; the scheduled-queue table has no generic route.
Both paths take their read floor and writable fields from one shared rules module, so a restriction cannot be added to one path and missed on the other.
writableFields excludes strike-vote, mandate, cost, status, confidentiality and agreement-link fields on create and update (400), and negotiations are read at steward level instead of member.

Every stored rule (active state, hours, blocked dates, durations, advance window, allowed roles, capacity, approval) is implemented as one tested pure function (19 tests). A first route that wired it to room_bookings was withdrawn before commit because the physical room_bookings table lacks 26 declared columns and the runtime role has no grant on it, so it could never have worked; the bookings path answers 501 until that exists.
items.remaining: Needs a reviewed migration that brings room_bookings to the declared shape (organization_id, booked_by, start_time, end_time, status and 21 more columns), RLS, and a storage-authority classification granting the runtime role access; then wire evaluateBooking into a bookings route under a room lock. lib/services/calendar-service.ts also still has an unused checkRoomAvailability stub that returns true.

items.explanation: The bookings path no longer edits the room row or exports PATCH or any room CRUD; it answers 501 for every method and reads or writes nothing.

batches.family: F01 Cron, scheduler and job results: one scheduled-job manifest, POST-only routes, one cron-secret rule, honest job results

items.explanation: All four aliases export POST only; so do the other ten scheduled routes (codemod f01-cron-post-only.cjs, idempotent). A contract test fails if any manifest route exports a method other than POST.

The manifest declares all 18 scheduled routes; apps.bicep generates one Container Apps schedule job per entry (POST with the cron secret, curl -f so a non-2xx fails the run). Compiles with az bicep; the contract test fails when a cron route is missing from the manifest or the bicep stops reading it.

One shared rule (x-cron-secret or bearer; CRON_SECRET_KEY then CRON_SECRET; unset never matches) used by withApi, verifyCronAuth, the rewards route and the edge check, which now compares in constant time over SHA-256 digests via WebCrypto (edge-safe) instead of !==. CRON_API_ROUTES is derived from the manifest.

The vercel.json entry (no method, no secret) is removed; calendar-sync is scheduled as a POST Container Apps job every 15 minutes, and verifyCronAuth now accepts the secret as a bearer token as well as x-cron-secret.
location-retention is an hourly POST Container Apps job generated from the manifest.

The route's own Authorization-only CRON_SECRET-only check is replaced by the shared rule, so one transport (x-cron-secret) satisfies the edge and the route; the edge compare is constant time; the GET handler is removed.

The calculation catch now records, logs and returns the failing organization; the save step returns the failing organization ids; the route answers 500 with counts and ids through jobResponse when any failed, and no longer runs markOverdueRemittances a second time.

An unknown task is a 400 that runs nothing; a rejected organization, an organization that resolves with success false, and an expiration batch whose own flag is false are failures; the run answers 500 naming the scopes; rejected errors serialise as text instead of {}.

The handler answers 500 for a run with any failed source and for the outer failure; every sync method writes the log row through syncLogOutcome: partial (not completed) when records failed, with the bounded collected error list in error_details.
billing-lifecycle is now a daily POST schedule job.
items.remaining: The route's generator still needs a session, so it cannot run headless; that needs its own review.

items.explanation: A run with failed session-reminder or expiry-warning sends answers 500 through jobResponse naming the failed batch, with the sent/failed counts and collected errors in the body; the message no longer claims success. The route writes nothing, so it is classified as a read-only POST for the audit ratchet.

batches.family: F01 Provider webhooks: Resend delivery events applied by rules, once, in one transaction

items.explanation: An event matching neither a message_log row nor a delivery-ledger row answers 404 retryable so the provider redelivers (covering an event that beats the sender storing the provider message id); a redelivery after the row exists applies it. Both are tested against PostgreSQL (pglite).

Status only advances to a higher rank (a late sent, delivered or opened never overwrites bounced, failed or complained); fact timestamps are filled when missing; existing metadata is preserved. The table comment no longer claims the log is immutable and states the real rule. Mutation-proved.

Each statistic counts a message at most once (a counted set persisted in message_log.metadata, seeded from timestamps and terminal status for older rows), and the campaign counters advance inside the UPDATE (jsonb || jsonb_build_object over the stored value) rather than from a value read earlier. Tested with redelivery and with a counter another writer already advanced. Mutation-proved.
A complaint or suppression now creates the preference row when none exists, writes a revoked consent record and the audit entry, and applies once per message in the same transaction.
items.remaining: Suppression is still scoped to the one organization on the message row; suppressing the same address in other organizations and in distribution-list subscriptions needs a cross-organization address-suppression design.

items.explanation: recordProviderCallback takes the caller's transaction (inserting inside a savepoint so a duplicate does not abort it); the webhook runs it in the same transaction as the message row, so a ledger failure rolls everything back and the retry repeats nothing. An unmatched or ambiguous ledger result is logged, and an event matching nothing is retried. Rollback proved with a failing audit write.

Migration 20261031 creates a unique (provider, provider_message_id) index when no pair repeats, otherwise a plain index with the duplicate count reported; both branches and idempotence executed on PostgreSQL (pglite). The webhook locks the row (FOR UPDATE) and refuses with 409 when two rows carry the id. Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

batches.family: F01 Provider webhooks: Shopify redemption lifecycle - one code format, shop-bound organization, retryable and idempotent, proportional refunds, no purchaser data

items.explanation: The code issued and the code parsed are defined together (shopify-redemption-rules): UE plus the 32 hex characters of the redemption id, lossless. The parser also accepts the dashed form and resolves a legacy 12-character code only as a prefix inside the shop's organization among redemptions awaiting payment, and only when exactly one matches, so codes already issued still complete. Round trip unit-tested; the full paid, fulfilled, refunded lifecycle runs against PostgreSQL (pglite).

A failure answers 500; an event that cannot be applied yet (a fulfilment or refund for an order not recorded as paid) answers 503 with Retry-After; neither records a receipt, so the redelivery is applied. A receipt is recorded only after the handler, only for a final outcome, and tolerates a concurrent duplicate. The handlers are idempotent on their own state (an order already applied is a success), so the separate receipt transaction cannot lose or double-apply an event. Mutation-proved.

A refund returns its share of the credits (floor of creditsSpent x refunded line-item subtotal / order line-item total), a later refund returns its own share, each Shopify refund id is applied once, the redemption becomes refunded only when everything spent has come back, and the total returned never exceeds the credits spent. Refunds are recorded in the stored payload and in the audit entry. Mutation-proved.

The receipt keeps only the topic, shop domain and the order or refund id; the redemption keeps order facts (number, currency, totals, product and variant ids, quantity, price) and no customer id, e-mail, name or line-item title; discount codes are no longer logged. Migration 20261102 irreversibly redacts what was already stored in webhook_receipts and reward_redemptions (executed on PostgreSQL pglite, repeatable).

Every lookup and write of the handler runs inside withRLSContext bound to the shop's organization, and the redemption's organization is checked against it. The organization comes from the shop domain through migration 20261101: a unique index on the lower-cased domain and a column-level SELECT (org_id, shop_domain) grant with a read-only policy for the system role; the token and secret references stay unreadable (executed with real roles and RLS on pglite). The runtime-role behaviour under the real application roles is still to be qualified on native PostgreSQL.

The shop domain header must belong to exactly one organization or the signed event is refused (403, logged), each shop has its own rate-limit allowance, and the pre-signature limit is keyed on one normalised address instead of the whole forwarded-for string.
items.remaining: The HMAC still uses one global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET for every organization; per-organization secrets (shopify_config.webhook_secret_ref) need the secret store. The address key is only as trustworthy as the front proxy that sets the header.

batches.family: F01 Scheduled jobs that alert or import: durable deduplicated alerts, one transaction per alert, paged and leased imports

items.explanation: The in-process bus events are replaced by a durable inbox alert for the steward each late or at-risk claim is assigned to, written inside that organization's own context and deduplicated by a unique index over (organization, user, claim+kind+deadline) from migration 20261103: a rerun, retry or overlapping run adds nothing; a new deadline or escalation alerts again. Unassigned claims are counted in the result. Real-SQL tested; mutation-proved (dedupe, recipient). Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

The scan is keyset-paged (500 per page, bounded page count that fails the run rather than truncating silently), each claim is assessed once, and the metrics are awaited with their failures reported through the job result (500 naming the organization). Metrics are keyed by organization and clock hour.
items.remaining: recordPilotMetricEvent does not deduplicate by trace id, so two runs in one hour still record two metric rows; an idempotency key needs support in @nzila/platform-pilot-metrics.

items.explanation: The rule, inbox notices, execution record and audit entry are all written on the sweep's transaction handle in one savepoint per signal (the module-level db handle is no longer used for writes). Proved on PostgreSQL: an audit failure leaves no inbox row and no execution for that alert while other organizations' alerts are kept, and the next run completes it.

The never-read pending notification_tracking row is no longer written and an execution records only the channel that delivered (in_app, with the recipient count) and its measured time. The alert goes to the organization's active administrators and president; an alert nobody can receive is a failed execution and a failed job (500), not a success. Reruns in the same hour alert nobody twice. No e-mail is sent or claimed; delivering alerts by e-mail is not part of this fix.

The Google import follows every page (250 per call, 50-page bound that fails instead of truncating), the cron passes the stored sync token (without the window and ordering Google rejects with one), a 410 falls back to a full sync, and the new token is stored only when every page was read and every event applied; otherwise the import throws and the connection is recorded as failed with a retry time. Per-event and token-store errors are no longer swallowed. The due connections are locked FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and leased for 15 minutes in the same transaction, each lease bound to the row's organization. Google only: the Microsoft import has the same shape and is not yet changed.

batches.family: F01 Rewards cron: atomic per-member awards, honest scheduled and expiration tasks, organization context and run audit

items.explanation: Repeat protection (an advisory lock per organization and award type, and a same-day NOT EXISTS over the member's awards in any state) was already in the source and is proven on PostgreSQL by anniversary-idempotency.pglite.test.ts (existing, not mine). What was still open is closed here: each member's create and issue is one savepoint, so a failure in either rolls both back and no approved award is left un-issued, one member's failure no longer aborts the others' work in the shared transaction, and the run reports failed members (success false) instead of a smaller count. Proved on PostgreSQL: a failed issue leaves no award for that member and the next run completes only that member.

The unused years-of-service scale and its helper are removed (credits are the award type's configured amount, which issueAward applies); the years are recorded in the award metadata. The reason text names the organization (read inside the transaction) instead of its UUID, tested on PostgreSQL. No years-of-service credit scale is applied: that would be a product decision on money, not a fix.

A scheduled rule names an award type and a cron expression but nothing that says who earns the award, so no award can be derived; the task now reports those rules as skipped (and logs a warning) and never as processed. Evaluating scheduled rules remains unbuilt; it is not claimed.

The three overlapping windows are replaced by exact-day tiers (30, 14 and 7 days out), so a daily run warns each earning once per tier; the warned amount is capped at what the member still holds and spent credits are not warned; a failed send makes the batch fail and is counted per organization. Proved on PostgreSQL and mutation-proved.
items.remaining: There is no sent record, so two runs on the same day (a retry, an overlap) mail the same member twice, and a missed day misses that tier; a durable per-earning-and-tier sent marker needs a table. Nothing in the product sets an expiry or writes an expire entry yet, so the task still has nothing to warn about.

items.explanation: The cron lists organizations under system authority and runs each organization's anniversary and scheduled task inside that organization's own RLS context, so the services' shared db handle is subject to row-level security on that path.
items.remaining: The wallet and redemption routes wrapped by withRoleAuth, and the expiration scan (a cross-organization read), still reach the shared handle without a tenant context; each needs its own routing.

items.explanation: Each organization's anniversary and scheduled run writes an audit entry (processed, failed or skipped, success) inside its own context, the organizations whose members were e-mailed get an audit entry with the sent and failed counts, an audit that cannot be written fails the run naming the organization, and a member's create and issue are one atomic unit.

batches.family: F01 remainder: ICRA authority and credentials, labour-standards and location erasure honesty, ML provenance, organization archival

items.explanation: The route already refuses an organization's own administrator (403, platform governance required) and gives even a platform administrator no direct archive (501, institutional lifecycle workflow required), so DELETE no longer archives. The source change was upstream's; the regression test proving it (admin refused, non-admin refused, platform admin 501, nothing written, no audit, malformed id 400) is new. The organization aggregate reads now accept both driver result shapes, which also repairs an upstream pglite test that read zero claims.

The paid-tier fulfilment now issues the single-use claim credential (32 random bytes, 30-day expiry, bound to the buyer e-mail) in the same transaction as the tier upgrade, guarded so an existing or consumed credential is never replaced, and a replayed delivery issues nothing.
items.remaining: Nothing delivers the credential to the buyer (the same gap exists for workbooks) and there is no ICRA claim page, so a buyer still cannot present it; delivery needs the e-mail sender and a claim route in the UI.

items.explanation: The shared cron secret no longer authorizes a review: the caller must be a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise, nothing written). The reviewer role is the verified governance_reviewer authority; a role asserted in the body is refused unless it matches, and the audit actor is the reviewer's own user id instead of a constant. For an unclaimed prospect assessment the reviewer's identity is still not persisted (no tenant to audit against, and the decision record has no reviewer field).

An update changes only the fields supplied: sending only a credential reference no longer disables the integration or clears its settings and webhook URL. Switching enabled through configure now carries the same IS NOT DISTINCT FROM concurrency predicate as the activate route (409 and no audit when the state changed), the row is read FOR UPDATE, and the audit records the resulting state, the previous state and which fields changed.

No source of minimum wage rates exists, so none is published: minimumWage is null with minimumWageStatus not_published instead of a zero rate that reads as a real one. Live rates are not provided by this change.

When there is no active consent to revoke, DELETE now erases whatever location tracking and geofence rows remain (consent expired or already withdrawn, an unfinished retention sweep) and audits the erasure; it answers 404 only when there is neither a consent to revoke nor data to erase, and then keeps no log row. revokeLocationConsent itself is unchanged.

The score is presented as a rule-based heuristic: no confidence, no interval and no training date are returned or stored. Its priority and time remaining are read from the case in the caller's organization (404 for a case that is not), so a caller can no longer choose the inputs that decide an imminent-breach alert; values sent for them are ignored.
items.remaining: The transition count and previous-breach flag are still caller-supplied (they add at most 0.34, so with a case that has time left they cannot reach the 0.80 alert threshold); deriving them needs the claim history.

items.explanation: ml_predictions moves from OPERATIONAL to READ_ONLY in the generic CRUD governance, so the six generic prediction routes can no longer insert or alter a prediction row; only the dedicated scoring routes write it. Covered by the existing governance and route-coverage ratchets.

batches.family: F02: paths that advertise an operation but were generic CRUD over an unrelated table, or placeholder context routes

items.explanation: Every route that was the generic CRUD factory over organization_members under a name that advertises another operation (admin alerts, dues, employment, job classifications, leaves, PKI, roles, segments, system settings, bulk import, member search and others) now answers HTTP 501 behind its original role floor. Only members/[id] still binds the roster table. A contract test fails if another route binds it again. The earlier behaviour (a roster listing presented as the operation, or a refused write) is removed rather than preserved.
admin/segments, its item and execute routes and admin/system/settings no longer present another table's rows as the operation; they answer 501.

equity/monitoring, self-identify and snapshots answered the generic factory over member_segments. Special-category equity data is neither collected nor monitored there, so they answer 501 and expose no segment rows.
support/metrics and support/sla answered notification rows as support figures; they answer 501.
The ticket collection, item, assign and comments routes answered the same notification rows (assign and comments were the item route); all answer 501.

The fourteen organizing routes named for assignments, card check, committee, forms, labour board, filings, notes, sequences, support percentage and workplace mapping were campaign-row CRUD. They answer 501 at the officer floor; only organizing/campaigns remains a campaign route.

continuity/inheritance answered the pre-signup pending_profiles table. It answers 501; the table is no longer bound, so its governance entry was removed (an unlisted table is refused by the fail-closed default). The route test that pinned the old factory configuration was rewritten to pin the 501.

onboarding/transfers re-exported the event recorder behind a guard that always passed; it answers 501. The test that asserted transfers delegated to the audited recorder (and returned 200) was replaced by an assertion that the route answers 501 and does not reuse the recorder.
onboarding/readiness wrapped the pending-profiles handlers behind a placeholder guard; it answers 501.
reports/[id]/share no longer exposes the report table; its DELETE can no longer remove a report. It answers 501 until a recipient grant exists.
upload answered a JSON insert of a media-library row that receives no file; it answers 501 so a posted file is never reported stored.

enterprise/integrations was the generic factory over oauth_providers (per-user provider ids and tokens, no organization); it answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed with its last binding.
The enterprise integrations path no longer answers an empty 200 for a caller without an organization; it answers 501.
events/[id]/occurrences was a byte-for-byte copy of the event item route; it answers 501.

The inheritance, archives and docs aliases (the pending-profile table and the document repository behind a guard that always returned true) all answer 501; the document repository itself is reached at /api/documents/repository.
org/current reads the caller's organization (name, slug, tier, enabled features) under its RLS context and answers 404 when there is no row, instead of a placeholder with a null name.
tenant/current answers 410 Gone, pointing at org/current. Its old route test (asserting the placeholder body) was deleted and superseded by the 410 test.

Access is the service key or a signed-in platform administrator (401 / 403 otherwise); the error text is logged, not returned. The existing queue-status test was adapted to mock the platform-admin guard and logger.
The catch-all already answers 410 for every method; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.
Same: 410 with no data body, upstream's change, existing test.
Carbon routes already answer 501; upstream's change, existing test.
The route already answers 501 with no organization row read or written; upstream's change, existing test.
Same as access-logs.
The case is verified against the organization (B08).
items.remaining: The case id is still not stored on the prediction row.

batches.family: F02: model and cognition output must come from the organization's records or be refused (501 / 400 / 502), never a constant or a reassuring default

items.explanation: The correlation engine already refuses with NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every organization; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

The systems-dynamics, governance-coherence, operational-coordination, operating-rhythm, multi-domain and operational-trust engines embedded fixed frequencies, response times, integration scores and narrative claims (for example "Consistent governance behavior") and presented them as measurements. They now fail with 501 through the same refusal as the correlation engine.
items.remaining: The response-elasticity and governance-momentum engines remain: they derive scores from counts of cognition-memory entries with arbitrary scaling. They hold no fixed claim, but the scaling is not a validated measure.

items.explanation: The default confidence of 60 is gone: an engine states a confidence only when it supplies one (otherwise 0), and the two remaining engines state evidence volume (cognition-memory entries analysed, capped at 100).
items.remaining: The explainability envelope's evidence and reasoning lists are still not populated by these engines.

items.explanation: A scenario that matches no node or role is refused with 400 instead of a canned low-severity result (impact 20, probability 85). Affected roles now select the nodes associated with them. The test that asserted the canned minimal result was replaced by tests for the refusal and for role selection.

The preset scenarios name roles and no nodes, so every one of them reached the canned minimal result. Roles are now honoured, and a preset that matches nothing in the organization is refused rather than modelled.

Model output is validated (non-empty summary, at most five handoff points); anything else is a 502 and nothing is stored. The former fallback text ("Manual review of source content is recommended") that was stored as a generated summary is gone, and its test was replaced.
Nothing is sent to the provider unless the retiring employee consented (409 otherwise); interviews above the restricted level go as confidential rather than internal.
The detector already reads only interviews selected by derivedAnalyticsCondition (published, consented, open levels), proved against real SQL by an existing test; that change was upstream's.

The churn route scored members with a randomly initialised network pre-trained on generated examples and stored the score. GET and POST now answer 501 behind the officer floor. The extensive route test, which exercised that scoring with mocks, was replaced by a test of the 501 and of the absence of the generated-example model. Two round-48 ratchet tests that pinned the former handler's organization-input properties (body schema without organizationId, organization-context check) were rewritten to assert that the route now accepts no organization input at all and touches no stored prediction.

ml/monitoring/drift, monitoring/usage, predictions/claim-outcome, predictions/timeline, predictions/workload-forecast and ml/recommendations were the generic factory over ml_predictions under six model names; all answer 501 and ml_predictions has no generic binding (its governance entry was removed). The monitoring alerts route (GET queried columns and a table that no schema defines and stated a fixed PSI 0.28 drift alert; POST wrote to a table no migration creates) also answers 501; its three POST tests were replaced by one assertion of the 501.
The route already reports error_rate as null and no longer names a claim count as a request count; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing test.

batches.family: F02: organization figures, report engine, signature, social analytics, satisfaction and settings answer from stored records or refuse

items.explanation: The member, grievance and growth figures now run under the organization named in the path (its own identity for a direct member, the system role with the exact organization predicate for a platform or parent administrator already authorized), not the caller's own organization, so a federation administrator no longer reads zeros for a local. Average resolution days and the growth rate are null, not 0, when they are undefined. A real-SQL test proves the figures for the officer and for the administrator above. The unit test mocks were adapted to the new call shape (child count first, one members query).

The children, descendants, ancestors, members and path routes already validate the id (400) and answer 404 for an organization the caller cannot read; the source change was upstream's and is covered by an existing real-SQL test.

POST /api/organizations stores description, province_territory, charter_number and affiliation_date; a value of the wrong shape or an impossible date is refused with 400 rather than dropped under a 201.
The tree read is bounded to the organizations the caller may read, ordered and limited (upstream), and now runs as the system role like the hierarchy route instead of the ambient connection role.

The route kept its own table allowlist, different from the registry the builder and executor use. It now validates against the executor's registry only, so one list governs data sources, fields, filters, joins, having and limits (the executor already resolved and bounded those). The route test mock now uses the real registry.

The executor reports a refused configuration (kind invalid) separately from a failed query (kind failed). The route answers 400 with the reason or 500, audits a validation failure or a failure, and never records an unsuccessful run as success or as an authentication failure. A database error message is no longer returned. Two executor tests that asserted the database message was returned were changed to assert it is not.

The registry named columns the tables do not have (claims.outcome, members first_name/last_name, deadlines current_deadline) and a joinable table that is not a source (claim_notes). They now map to the physical columns (resolution_outcome, due_date), the member name is the single field name, and a new ratchet fails if a registry column is not a physical column of its table. A saved report that named first_name or last_name is refused rather than run against a missing column.

The built-in provider generated envelope ids and sign URLs, stored and sent nothing, and reported every envelope as sent. It is removed: the default provider is a configured DocuSign or HelloSign account or a 501, and the document route refuses any other provider name. The tests of the stub were removed and replaced by tests that there is no built-in provider and no stub fallback.
items.remaining: Documents already stored with provider "internal" keep that value; their status sync reports provider_unavailable and their void is attempted against no provider.

items.explanation: fetchAnalytics fetched platform responses it never transformed and returned an empty list as a success. It now answers 501 when nothing was collected, and the analytics read says (data_collected, message) whether analytics were ever collected instead of letting an empty range read as no activity.
items.remaining: No collector transforms the Meta, Instagram, Twitter or LinkedIn responses into the analytics table, and nothing calls fetchAnalytics, so no figure exists yet.

items.explanation: The directory route is a member-safe projection for members, full rows (audited) for officers, and answers 405 to writes; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
A representative with no completed surveys, or an unknown id, is a 404 rather than 200 with zero averages; a caller with no organization is refused rather than reading across organizations.

A survey can only be created for a resolved or closed claim (409 otherwise), and a claim with no assigned representative is refused (400) instead of accepting any representative id. The existing test fixtures were given a claim status and extended with the new refusals.

name (1-200), shortName (at most 50) and provinceTerritory (at most 100) are validated before anything is read; a missing body or organization is a 400, not a server error. The settings merge reads the row under FOR UPDATE and writes in the same transaction, and a missing row is a 404 with no audit.

batches.family: F02: invoices, CBA export and comparison, committee intelligence, dispatch, ICRA checkout, onboarding, reconciliation, testimonials and vocabulary state only what they do

items.explanation: An external invoice is a copy of a provider record, and nothing ingests one. The collection keeps its mandate-checked read; POST answers 501 instead of writing a hand-made financial row through the generic factory, and the table's governance entry was removed with its last binding. The round-39 cohort ratchet that required a crud-factory route for the table was rewritten to require the mandate-checked read and the absence of the factory.
items.remaining: The storage-authority manifest still lists INSERT for the tenant runtime role on external_invoices, which nothing in the tenant runtime now uses; reducing it needs a grant migration and is not done.

items.explanation: The route generated a platform invoice and delivered nothing. It answers 501 behind the steward floor (generation remains POST /api/finance/invoices and the billing batch). Its test, which asserted the generation, was replaced by an assertion of the 501 and of the absence of the generator.

The export asked for 10000 rows but the list serves at most 100 a page, so the file silently held the first page. It reads every page and refuses (400) a result set over 10000, naming the count, instead of cutting it.

The GET stub (a 200 with a usage hint) is removed (405). commonKeywords is now computed from the compared clause texts (words of four letters or more, not stop words, present in every clause, ranked by frequency; English and French). Clause ids are validated as ids and a malformed body is a 400. The route test fixtures use real ids now.

POST stored a snapshot whose summary said synthesis was pending and whose themes, positions and recommendations were empty. It checks authority and then answers 501; nothing is stored. The snapshot list is unchanged.

The route served a table no route writes and nothing enforces under the name of an employer data firewall. It answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed. The writeRole test for the route was rewritten to assert the 501 and the absence of the table binding, and the committed schema mutation program was regenerated because the table is now unreachable from any route.

An assignment accepted any member ids for a request in any state, in any number, with no check that they were members, and counted the request filled from the ids of one call. It now requires an open or partly filled request of the caller's organization (row locked), active members of that organization, no worker already offered or placed, and no more offers than workers requested, with a distinct status for each refusal. Proven on real SQL. Three mock-chain tests of assignWorkersToDispatch were removed because the mocks cannot express these queries; the pglite suite replaces them.
items.remaining: rankCandidates still scores a candidate list nothing supplies (no source of member skills or availability), and the assignment is an officer's explicit selection, not engine-ranked.

items.explanation: A failed query is an error and the member count is null for an ordinary member, not zero; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
The export answers 501 in every environment; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
The report gate accepts submitted as well as completed, so a paid report is no longer refused for a status nothing writes; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

Checkout now reads the assessment status and answers 409 with no Stripe session unless the assessment is submitted or completed, so a buyer is never charged for a report the report route would refuse.
The public configuration no longer reports credentialsStored: true for every integration: it reports false, with credentialsResolvable false, because only a reference is held.
items.remaining: A credentialRef is still accepted and stored and nothing resolves it to a secret; a vault-backed resolution path does not exist.

items.explanation: The bookings route answers 501 and reads and writes nothing; the booking rules are implemented and tested in room-booking-rules.ts.
items.remaining: The physical room_bookings table lacks the columns the application declares and has no runtime grant; booking needs that migration before the rules can be wired in.

items.explanation: The sector now scores (25, case-insensitive match against the federation's sectors) and "Similar size" is stated only when the smaller count is at least half the larger. The reason text "Similar size category", which was given for any ratio, is gone and its test was changed to the new text.

The route served a literal table of features, integrations and limits by organization type that nothing defines or applies. It answers 501; its test of the table was replaced by an assertion of the 501.

For an organization run, the period is locked, a billing period named in the request must be the organization's own (404), and a second run for the same period is refused (409, naming the earlier run) instead of adding a second set of exceptions. A period that ends before it starts is refused. The existing mocked test of a run gained the two new checks in its queue; three tests were added.
items.remaining: The service still accepts a run with no organization, which reconciles every organization together; no route uses that mode, but it is not removed.

items.explanation: The component sent status, reviewedAt, reviewedBy, rejectionReason and isFeatured; the table has approvedAt and featured only. It now sends those, the route stamps the approval with the server clock once, and the reject flow is removed because the table cannot record a rejection (the component has no importer).

The six vocabulary routes serve identifiers, labels, descriptions and categories only. Service-level hours, escalation, legal and settlement flags, role permissions, default priority and severity, and status transitions are no longer served as institutional reference data; the case state machine still reads them from the package server-side.

batches.family: F03: platform-wide datasets are changed only with platform authority; an organization's role floor is not authority over rows every organization reads

items.explanation: The extracted CBA dataset (agreements, findings, wage adjustments, clauses, sources, ingestion) has no organization column. Extraction, ingestion (create, run, seed) and source create/update were open to an organization's administrator; each now calls requireSystemAdmin() first. A contract test checks all seven mutating handlers. The extraction route test gained the platform-admin mock and a refusal test.

The review queue and review decisions (approve, reject, supersede) changed rows every organization reads at the steward floor of any one organization. Both methods now require a platform administrator and the reviewer role recorded is platform_administrator, not a literal "steward". A refusal test covers the queue and the decision, which write and read nothing.
Writes and review are now platform authority. The dataset is shared by design (no organization column), so a tenant predicate does not apply to its reads.
items.remaining: Reads (agreements list and detail, benchmark, documents, freshness) remain open to any entitled member or steward of any organization; whether the shared dataset may be read that widely, and under which entitlement, is an institutional decision.

items.explanation: The collection and item routes already require the platform content_manager role to write; upstream's change, now pinned by a contract test.
Case-study writes need content_manager and the item route (read and write) is limited to it; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.
The public list is limited to public, already published rows for both the rows and the count, and a status other than published is refused; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.
Proposals are scoped through their negotiation (parentScope), because the table has no organization column; upstream's change, pinned by a contract test.

batches.family: F03: a route reads and writes the caller's own organization; a target taken from the request is the caller's own or not found

items.explanation: Both routes compare or suggest for the caller's own organization. A target named in the query or body that is not the caller's reads as 404 and nothing is read; a caller with no organization is refused. Peer benchmarks now work without naming a target. The peer-benchmarks test that required an organizationId parameter was replaced by three tests of the new behavior; the suggest-clauses fixtures use the caller's organization.
The roster excludes removed members and is read a page at a time (default and maximum 200) in a stable order; proven on real SQL, including that consecutive pages do not overlap.
The SCIM list excludes removed members, counts and pages in SQL from the requested start index, and no longer loads the whole roster.
Provisioning creates a pending membership, not an active one, so naming a user grants no access until the person accepts.
items.remaining: The userName string is still stored as the membership user id; binding it to a verified identity needs the identity-to-profile mapping.

items.explanation: The pending list is bound to the caller's organization as well as the member; the route refuses a caller with no organization.
The trends read the authenticated organization only, as predicate and RLS binding; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
Platform-wide counters are for a platform administrator or the service key only; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
The service key is compared in constant time and no error text is returned; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
The churn route answers 501 and reads no claims (batch B10), so its second identity resolution and unscoped claim read no longer exist.
The alerts route answers 501 and reads nothing (batch B10).
Discovery already lists federations only for an officer-floor caller and (batch B12) now scores the sector.
items.remaining: It remains a directory of federations by name and member count, readable by any organization's officer; whether that directory may be shown to every organization is an institutional decision.

batches.family: F04: generic-CRUD facades advertising another capability answer 501 behind their original role floor

items.explanation: clc/dashboard, clc/remittances and clc/sync served clc_sync_log rows under dashboard, remittance and sync names; all answer 501. Their tables lost their last generic binding, so the governance entries for grievances, clc_sync_log, cms_media_library, cms_pages and organizer_tasks were removed (an unlisted table is refused by the fail-closed default); the "keeps grievances as OWN_ROWS_READ" case was removed from the governance test for that reason.
clauses/search listed the clause table without searching; it answers 501.

Certificate generation, renewal reminders, completion certificates and notification preferences were the training-course factory; all answer 501. The admin certification manager that posts to renewal-reminders now receives the 501 instead of a course row.

cope/canvassing and cope/officials served donation-campaign rows; they answer 501. cope/campaigns, the legitimate campaign collection, is unchanged. The canvassing interface component now receives the 501.
exports, its item, csv, excel and pdf routes were report-definition CRUD that produced no file; all answer 501.
Affiliates, dashboard, meetings and remittances under a federation were copies of the federation item route; all answer 501.
federations/benchmark/grievances answered grievance rows as a benchmark; it answers 501.
locals and locals/[id] served bargaining units as local unions; both answer 501.
The locals routes no longer write bargaining-unit fields at the steward floor; they answer 501.
jurisdiction/clc-compliance and validate-deadline served bargaining-unit rows with no validation; both answer 501. The deadline calculation paths the UI uses are separate routes and are unchanged.
healthwelfare/plans answered the per-capita remittance ledger under a plan name at the member floor; it answers 501.
movement-insights/trends served stored analytics rows, not the consent-gated aggregate the dashboard uses; it answers 501.
organizer/impact served organizer task rows as impact metrics; it answers 501.
portal/documents served CMS pages with no portal principal; it answers 501.
portal/documents/upload received no file and stored a caller-written URL; it answers 501, so no URL is stored.
storage/usage and storage/cleanup served media-library rows and computed or deleted nothing; both answer 501.
reports/[id]/run and reports/[id]/execute were the report item route, so their DELETE removed the report; both answer 501. Ad-hoc execution is POST /api/reports/execute.

Search, citations and documents under arbitration precedents were the decision table or copies of its item route; all answer 501. The writerole test for those three routes was replaced by assertions of the 501 and of the absence of the table binding; the precedents collection and item keep their content_manager write role.
support/metrics answers 501 (batch B09), so a steward can no longer store a notification for any user through it.

batches.family: F09/F10: payment initiation is idempotent, exports are formula-safe, and routes named for an intake or feed that does not exist answer 501

items.explanation: Initiation is server-owned (no client amount, organization or member) and returns the same open payment for a repeated or concurrent call, cancelling and reopening only when the balance changed; upstream's change, covered by an existing real-SQL test.
The balance reads the authenticated member and organization from the session only and never fabricates a balance when there is no ledger activity; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
A credit balance is reported when posted payments exceed posted charges; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.
The export neutralises formula cells, is bounded, role-checked and audited in the reading transaction; upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

reconciliation/bank and reconciliation/upload listed runs and exceptions under names promising a bank feed and a file intake; both answer 501 behind the officer floor. The upload route test, which asserted the exception list, was replaced by an assertion of the 501.
In production a missing NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is a 503 with no Stripe session instead of a redirect to localhost.
items.remaining: The charged amount comes from a Stripe price id or a built-in default and is not compared with the price the page displays.

batches.family: F05: inputs are typed and bounded, empty data is refused rather than scored, and constants are not confidence

items.explanation: An organization with no dependency data is refused (409) instead of being scored by divisions by zero or by the absence of risks never looked for, with or without interviews. Tests: the refusal for both cases and finite scores once a dependency map exists.
Both engine wrappers (foundational and dynamics) no longer state a constant confidence of 60: it is the evidence the payload reports reading, capped at 100, or 0.
items.remaining: The explainability envelope's evidence and reasoning lists are still not populated by these engines.

items.explanation: The operational-trust engine, which scored out of range and stated "moderate" with no data, answers 501 (batch B10).
The governance-coherence engine, which embedded literal scores, answers 501 (batch B10).
items.remaining: The governance-momentum engine still derives scores from ratios of cognition-memory entry counts with arbitrary scaling.

items.explanation: The coordination, rhythm and trust engines answer 501 (batch B10).
items.remaining: The response-elasticity engine still derives its indicators from entry counts and labels them elasticity.

items.explanation: The churn route answers 501 and contains no SQL (batch B10).
The churn route performs no invocation audit write at all now that it answers 501 (batch B10).
The alerts route answers 501 and contains no SQL (batch B10).

The body is parsed with a bounded schema (userName 1-320, names at most 100, at most 10 well-formed e-mails); malformed, oversized or non-JSON input is a 400 naming the field, with nothing written or audited.
The exception list validates every status against the vocabulary (400 otherwise, before any query), is ordered and bounded at 200. The run list route (reconciliation/bank) answers 501.
The run lookup is bound to the caller's organization (another organization's run reads as not found); upstream's change, covered by an existing test.

batches.family: F06: a read does not write, an effect is audited with its record, and a state is recorded only when the effect it names happened

items.explanation: GET computes and returns a benchmark and refuses ?save. Saving a snapshot is a new POST that needs a platform administrator (the dataset has no organization column), records the intent before the write, and stores nothing when that audit cannot be written.
No route or cognition library writes the local file system any more (upstream's change); a contract test now fails if one does.
Same: the read routes no longer write files, so there is no write to audit separately; pinned by the contract test.

Every route under /api/ai calls a feature gate, the AI safety check and a rate limit (upstream's change); a contract test fails if a new AI route lacks one. cache-stats is platform-administrator only and audited.

A provider failure while voiding is no longer swallowed: the document is not recorded as voided and no void is audited, and the sender is told with a conflict, because the envelope can still be signed at the provider.

Signing now refuses an expired request and, when sequential signing is set, a signer whose earlier signers have not all signed; the signer must already be the authenticated platform user. The mocked drizzle-orm in the service test gained lt.
items.remaining: The stored requireAuthentication flag is not given a second factor: signing relies on the platform session only.

items.explanation: The roster is read only by stewards and above, the administrators above the organization and the platform; a member, a suspended member and a stranger are refused (upstream's change, proven on real SQL).

Only an allow-listed set of non-secret preference keys is accepted; authority keys (per-capita rate, credits, remittance day, renewal date, telephone number) are refused with 400 and nothing is saved or audited (upstream's change, covered by existing tests; the merge is now transactional, batch B11).
Members receive a member-safe projection of active assignments; only officers receive the full rows, and that read is audited (upstream's change, covered by an existing test).
The campaign route reads and writes at the officer floor; upstream's change, pinned by an existing test.

batches.family: F01/F03/F05/F04/F12: truthful pilot bootstrap, bounded social reads, typed campaigns, fail-closed remote media

items.explanation: Existing fixture-slug organizations now require a durable route-origin marker before bootstrap/reset, and reset preserves all onboarding checklist rows. Non-fixture members and grievances are refused before deletion. This is containment, not a fully governed safe reset.
items.remaining: Per-row immutable fixture provenance, changed fixture-row protection, related-record handling, dry-run and independent approval are still absent.

items.explanation: The response now reports zero worksites actually written and separately identifies unseeded fixture worksites; member and grievance counts use INSERT RETURNING, not attempts; onboarding uses the seven canonical persisted checklist IDs and no invented completed tasks.
Social post pagination rejects NaN, negative, fractional, oversized, zero-limit and malformed values before SQL, with a maximum page of 100 and offset of 10,000.

Campaign creation now validates recognized goal metrics and status and persists impressions, engagement rate, conversions and requested status in real columns. Unsupported/duplicate goals and unknown fields are refused instead of being silently discarded.

Campaign updates now pass through a strict typed schema, reject unknown/privileged fields and invalid status/platforms, and persist validated goal columns rather than passing untrusted body values to SQL.

Removed all arbitrary server-side X media URL fetching and uploading; the route explicitly refuses remote media ingestion while retaining text-only X publishing. Regression cases cover metadata IPs, loopback, redirects and file schemes without invoking fetch.
items.remaining: Secure verified-asset ingestion and an approved media-publishing journey must be built before X media publishing is available.

batches.family: F07: a role floor is eligibility, not authority; reads and writes need the mandate, ownership, sensitivity or workflow that the record belongs to

items.explanation: The provider list (issuer, endpoints, client id, attribute mapping) is an administrator read; credential columns were already reduced to a boolean.

The diagnostic is a platform administrator's: anyone else gets 403 and the backend is never called; the response carries backend statuses only, never the backend bodies. Test disclosure: two tests added, the existing one now mocks platform-admin authority.
Report definitions (which sources and filters a report reads) are read at the steward floor, not by any member. No UI consumes these collection routes.

The templates route no longer fronts the whole report table: it lists only rows marked as templates with an allow-listed projection, and a create is always stored as an organization template through a strict body schema, in the tenant context and audited.
The registry is served at the officer floor, the same floor that can execute a report over it.
The committee routes omit the internal notes and custom fields from every response.
Internal working fields are no longer returned to every member.
items.remaining: A committee is still listed to every member of the organization: there is no committee-membership scope on the generic read.

items.explanation: alertRecipients (user ids and emails of staff notified) is omitted from every KPI response.
Negotiations are read at the steward floor through shared rules (upstream's change); bargaining proposals, which carry unreleased positions, now match it.
The realtime alert inbox needs an officer, since each execution carries the rule's trigger data.
The joint health-and-safety committee roster is read at the steward floor.
SMS messages and conversations are read and written at the officer floor.
SMS campaigns are read and written at the officer floor.

The generic factory gained belowStaffReadCondition, applied to GET for a caller below the steward floor. Surveys add status != draft, so a member reads published surveys only; staff still read drafts.
The responses route exports POST only and its header states no individual identity, address or response row is returned to a steward; no read exposes respondents (upstream's change).
The factory gained staffReadsAll: with an owner column, a steward or above reads every member's registration or certification on GET while a member keeps their own; writes keep the owner scope.
The virtual-meeting access code, session budget and actual cost are omitted from every session response.
items.remaining: The factory has no per-role column view, so staff also cannot read the cost columns through this route.

items.explanation: A member reads only active courses; draft and archived ones are visible to staff.
A campaign body is limited to an allow-list; the amount raised, the status and the payment-provider identifiers can no longer be set by a steward.
A PATCH can no longer set status, closure, verification, investigation outcome or scoring fields on incidents, hazards and inspections.
items.remaining: No dedicated workflow route yet performs the investigation, verification and closure transitions that the blocked fields now require.

items.explanation: The PPE register, which names the member each item is issued to, is read at the health-and-safety representative floor.
A single-flag probe answers only flags the application defines (plus pilot-mode); an unknown name is a 404 and is not evaluated.

Connecting and disconnecting a publishing identity, and its OAuth callback, need an administrator; the business-management and organization-admin scopes are no longer requested; a connection is made only when the account manages exactly one Page, instead of picking the first.

An unparseable or malformed model answer now throws ExpertiseExtractionError; publish records the failed extraction and stores no score. Test disclosure: the test that asserted the default medium profile was replaced by two that assert refusal.
Reads of interviews apply the sensitivity floor and consent condition (upstream's change), proven on real SQL by an existing test.
Only a level that permits indexing is copied to the knowledge base, without the employee's name; sensitivity and consent travel with the source id (upstream's change, existing test).

A new interview is created at the restricted level (UNRECORDED_LEVEL) instead of the public_internal column default; an administrator classifies it through the governance step, and publication refuses an unclassified level.

The analytics aggregate takes a content-derived risk score only from interviews that are published, consented and at a derived-analytics level; the other derived views already read through that condition. The analytics test mocks the database, so the CASE expression is not exercised against real SQL.
items.remaining: The analytics SQL expression has no real-database test.

items.explanation: The succession analyzer selects interviews through the derived-analytics condition before anything reaches a model (upstream's change, existing test).
The topic graph reads interviews through the derived-analytics condition (upstream's change, existing test).
